what: Round 6 design stage (workflow wf_47873c46-dd7): research of public night scalpers, two independent declarations (faithful, simple), the judge's final declaration; nothing computed on prices

scalpers.name: Night Scalper Multi (MQL5 Code Base 16350, AM2 / Andrey Kornishkin, MT5, free source, 2016-2017)
scalpers.window: I read the source in full. New trades are allowed from the 'Start' hour (19:00 for the USDCAD and NZDUSD presets, 20:00 for GBPUSD) until midnight, terminal time. Any open position is closed at the first new chart bar after 00:00 terminal time. The terminal's GMT offset is not stated. On the usual GMT+2/+3 'New York close' broker clock this is 12:00/13:00-17:00 New York, with the forced exit exactly at the 17:00 NY rollover. That is the US afternoon up to the close, not the Asian night.
scalpers.pairs: Presets for USDCAD, GBPUSD and NZDUSD (up to 9 symbols). Checked once per new bar of the chart timeframe (H1 in the author's tests).
scalpers.entry: Bollinger Bands on the chart timeframe, current bar. Buy at market if Ask < lower band; sell if Bid > upper band. Only allowed when the band width (upper minus lower) is below 'Razmah' points, which acts as a narrow-channel gate. One position per symbol. Presets: USDCAD BB(40,1) with width < 450 points; GBPUSD BB(8,1) < 200; NZDUSD BB(4,1.2) < 450.
scalpers.exit: Fixed TP of 20/80/40 points (2/8/4 pips on 5-digit quotes). Fixed SL of 370/450/410 points (37/45/41 pips), so the stop is 5 to 18 times the target. Forced market close after midnight.
scalpers.filters: Only the band-width cap. No spread, weekday, news or rollover filter.
scalpers.real_evidence: None. There is only an optimisation screenshot (Jan-Sep 2016, H1). The GitHub file NightScalper.mq5 (KonzACDC/MQL5_MT5_EA) is byte-identical to this code. StockSharp sample 2343 is a port with the same defaults (USDCAD preset). Neither is independent evidence.

scalpers.name: MQL5 article 4102 'Night trading during the Asian session: How to stay profitable' (D. Zabudskiy, Jan 2018, code in the article)
scalpers.window: Code default is 22:00-03:00 terminal time, wrapping midnight. The offset is not stated; on a GMT+2/+3 NY-close clock that is 15:00-20:00 NY. The optimised run used 01:00-11:00 Moscow time (UTC+3), which is 22:00-08:00 UTC: 18:00-04:00 NY in winter, 17:00-03:00 NY in US summer. All positions are closed when the window ends.
scalpers.pairs: EURUSD on M30 is the main test. AUDUSD, GBPUSD, NZDUSD, USDCAD and USDCHF were also tested. The author found EURUSD, NZDUSD and AUDUSD 'most suitable'.
scalpers.entry: Bollinger Bands (default 12 periods, 2 SD; optimised period 11), current bar. Sell when the ask is within a few points of the upper band; buy when the bid is within a few points of the lower band (touch zone set by div_work/div_signal). An opposite signal closes the trade and reverses it.
scalpers.exit: Fixed TP and SL in points (defaults 50/100; optimised TP 120, SL 140 = 12/14 pips). Everything is closed at the end of the window.
scalpers.filters: Weekday switches (the optimised run skips Tuesday). No spread, news or rollover filter. Costs are not discussed.
scalpers.real_evidence: Backtest only (Halifax, 2017, AUD 100 deposit). About +152% on 'OHLC on M1' against +48% on real ticks. The author blames history quality for the gap and calls the band signals 'not accurate enough'. No live record.

scalpers.name: MQL5 article 1373 'How Reliable is Night Trading?' (S. Shashev, Aug 2013, template EA in the article)
scalpers.window: The night flat is taken as 18:00-10:00 server time. The template trades from h_beg = 20:00 to h_end = 10:00 server. The server offset is not stated and the article was written on a Russian-broker clock, so the NY conversion is uncertain (13:00-03:00 NY if the clock is GMT+2/+3 NY-close).
scalpers.pairs: EURCHF, EURCAD and GBPCAD, named as the night pairs that Alpari PAMM night accounts traded in 2012-2013.
scalpers.entry: At 20:00, the 'flat boundaries' are the highest high and lowest low of the two previous bars. Sell at market when Bid goes above that high; buy when Ask goes below that low. At most one buy and one sell per night: the author says a second entry 'often results in closing with a loss by the end of the night flat'.
scalpers.exit: TP 'quite close, from 10 to 50 points' (code: 20 points from the boundary). SL 'greater than TP, from 30 to 70 points' (code default 90). Everything is closed at h_end.
scalpers.filters: Time only. The author lists volatility analysis, news (intervention risk) and the underlying majors as improvements still needed.
scalpers.real_evidence: The author claims it 'earned around 50% per annum over 6 months' on a real account, with no statement shown. His practical findings: night spreads are 1.5-2x wider on EURCHF, GBPCAD and EURCAD. The EURCAD target had to be cut from 40 to 20 points between winter and summer. 'Night trading offers good profit opportunities in winter', less in spring and summer. Interventions on EURCHF/USDCHF can bring large losses.

scalpers.name: PolyFitScalper v1.57 (igorad, forex-tsd 2009, open source, reposted on the MQL5 forum)
scalpers.window: Alpari UK server, on UK time (GMT+0 winter / GMT+1 summer, i.e. New York + 5 h). StartHour 22 and EndHour 8 give 17:00-03:00 New York; Friday ends at 22:00 server. The default Schedule1.txt narrows trading to hand-picked slots, for example 21:30-22:50, 00:45-01:15, 01:30-01:45, 02:30-02:50, 04:15-06:00 and 06:30-06:55 server (16:30-17:50, 19:45-20:15, 20:30-20:45, 21:30-21:50, 23:15-01:00 and 01:30-01:55 NY), plus 19:15-20:15 (14:15-15:15 NY).
scalpers.pairs: EURGBP on M1 by default; a second set for EURCHF on M1. GBPCHF is mentioned.
scalpers.entry: A linear regression line (polynomial degree 1) over the last 150 M1 closes, with bands at +/-3.0 standard deviations (up to 3.7). Buy when Ask is below the lower band; sell when Bid is above the upper band. Up to 3 positions are layered at 3.0/3.35/3.7 sigma, a limited form of averaging.
scalpers.exit: Close when price returns to the middle line (ProfitRatio 0.5), once profit is at least 1 pip and the trade is at least 1.5 minutes old. Initial SL 45 pips. Optional fixed close time.
scalpers.filters: The schedule file sets minute-level hours per weekday. The author recommends a low-spread broker and ships a spread meter. No news filter.
scalpers.real_evidence: Only demo forward tests posted in the thread (2009). Useful mainly as an explicit example of curve-fitted night hours.

scalpers.name: Night Hunter Pro (Valeriia Mishchenko, MQL5 Market MT4 66358 / MT5 68327, June 2021, 2,800 USD)
scalpers.window: Server clock GMT+2 with US DST ('used by most brokers'), so 00:00 server = 17:00 NY. The order hours are hidden behind a 'Smart Time Filter' and not published. A third-party review says about 21:00-01:00 broker time (14:00-18:00 NY); this is unverified. A Friday stop hour of 22:00 server (15:00 NY) is recommended to avoid holding over the weekend. The signals show an average holding time of 11 h.
scalpers.pairs: EURUSD, GBPUSD and EURCHF are the '3 best' ('most liquid ... night scalping usually works best on these pairs'). Also USDCAD, USDCHF, CHFJPY, AUDCAD, EURCAD, EURAUD. M5, run from one chart.
scalpers.entry: Pending (limit) buy and sell orders placed around price at night. 'Minimum Price Range' is the minimum distance between the buy and sell pending orders, in % of ATR (0-20). The exact level logic is not disclosed.
scalpers.exit: Take profit ('most of the trades are closed using TP'). Fixed SL in pips, set per pair, which can be hidden. A close on floating drawdown. A Friday close.
scalpers.filters: A max spread for pending orders (cancels them) and a separate one for closing. A rollover time filter. A news filter. A negative-swap filter (no Wednesday-evening trades in the negative-swap direction). A Christmas/New Year filter. A cap on net exposure to the same currency (2 recommended). Splitting orders to limit slippage (single entries of at most 0.2 lot).
scalpers.real_evidence: Real IC Markets signals. 856903 '9 pairs', since 2020-10-27: 2,587 trades, 67.9% winners, PF 1.21, average win 0.65 against average loss 1.15 AUD (one loss = 1.8 wins), +195% with no deposits (about 1.5%/month), balance drawdown 21.9%. 856907 'all pairs': 2,185 trades, 67.6% winners, PF 1.22, +139%. Four other advertised signals (856906, 1046432, 1067804, 1067812) no longer exist. Several product reviews report losses after 2022.

scalpers.name: Scalp IC Markets ECN (MQL5 signal 683917, MT4) and Scalp IC Markets MT5 (signal 1560883), Roman Kartezhnikov - rules not published
scalpers.window: Not published. The description says 'Night scalping ... a virtual stop loss is applied at about rollover time due to greatly increased spreads'. A subscriber review (Oct 2026) says the system 'operates around the market rollover period (late night / market close and open)'. Average holding time is 2 h (1 h on the MT5 account), about 5 trades per week.
scalpers.pairs: Deals on 683917: GBPCAD 740, EURAUD 453, EURSGD 348, EURCAD 189, GBPUSD 154, CHFJPY 133, XAUUSD 132, USDCAD 125, EURGBP 125, GBPAUD 95, EURUSD 90, EURCHF 63, AUDCAD 36. The MT5 account trades GBPCAD, GBPAUD, EURSGD, EURAUD, GBPUSD, EURCAD, EURGBP, AUDCAD, XAUUSD, CHFJPY, AUDNZD.

scalpers.exit: 'Each order has its own fixed stop loss ... and take profit', with a hidden (virtual) stop around the rollover spike.

MT5 account since 2022-06-08: 2,637 trades, 72.65% winners, PF 1.58, average 0.65 against 1.09 EUR, equity drawdown 32.9%. A subscriber's copy test found a tracking error of about 1 pip at 3x size, about 4 pips at 8x and 8-12 pips at 20x. This is the longest clean public record of a night scalper found.

scalpers.name: Luna AI PRO (Profalgo Limited / Wim Schrynemakers, MT4 101970, July 2023; successor of the delisted 'Night Owl' 68713/84775)
scalpers.window: Start and stop times are set on GMT+2 winter / GMT+3 US-summer broker time, 'assuming rollover at 0:00', i.e. referenced to 17:00 NY. The default hours are not published. A per-pair rollover filter has its own start and end times. Options exist for Friday evening and the weekly open. Average holding on the signal is 4 h.
scalpers.pairs: EURAUD, EURCAD, EURCHF, GBPCHF, AUDUSD, AUDCAD, EURGBP, GBPAUD (the signal now trades EURAUD, AUDUSD, AUDCAD, GBPAUD). M5.
scalpers.entry: A 'mean-reverse strategy' that uses Bollinger Bands (the manual's error message names the indicator). Limit orders by default, or a market order if the limit is out of range. Levels are not disclosed.
scalpers.exit: SL and TP per pair; the TP can be moved by X pips, and SL/TP can be set after the fill to avoid levels distorted by slippage.
scalpers.filters: Max spread to enter. A spread level at which pending orders are deleted. A rollover filter for pairs with big rollover slippage. A cap on correlated trades (3 suggested). US holidays skipped. A triple-swap / maximum swap-cost filter. A news filter (including AUD pairs on JPY news). Per-pair lot reduction when a pair performs badly.
scalpers.real_evidence: Real IC Markets MT5 signal 1502590, public since 2022-04-27 (history from 2018): 2,533 trades, 88.9% winners, PF 1.24, average win 2.15 against average loss 13.94 USD (one loss = 6.5 wins), worst trade -194.52, balance drawdown 46.8%, +239% (about 1.3%/month). Most of this record falls in the lab's 2022-2026 validation and holdout years.

scalpers.name: SFE Night Scalper (vendor 'atractor'; MQL5 product 12156, now delisted) - independent review and Dukascopy backtests by ForexBenchmark (2019)
scalpers.window: Per-pair lists of server hours on a NY-close clock: hour 0 (00:00-01:00 = 17:00-18:00 NY) for most pairs, hours 0-1 for some, and 21-0/21-1/21-2 (14:00 to 17:00/18:00/19:00 NY) for CHFJPY, EURAUD and EURCHF. The reviewer: 'The most important timeframe for this strategy is the hour directly after the rollover, when the spreads are the highest. All pairs trade here and only a few trade before or right after this hour.'
scalpers.pairs: AUDUSD, AUDCAD, CADCHF, CHFJPY, EURAUD, EURCHF, EURNZD, EURUSD, EURCAD, EURGBP, GBPCAD, GBPUSD, USDCAD, USDCHF, USDJPY, USDSGD; another set adds GBPAUD, GBPCHF, GBPNZD, NZDCAD. M5.
scalpers.entry: 'Mean-reversion strategy on M5 time frame'; enters with pending orders. Levels are not disclosed.
scalpers.exit: Partial exits on many trades. SL/TP levels not disclosed.
scalpers.filters: Hours set per pair. No news filter.
scalpers.real_evidence: The vendor's live myfxbook account had 'over 4 years' of history in 2019 (myfxbook returned 403 here, so not read). The reviewer's Dukascopy tick backtests, 2010-2019, at 0.1 lot with vendor settings: hour-0 PF 0.71 (USDSGD), 0.97 (EURNZD), 1.09-1.48 for most pairs, 1.64 (EURAUD); hour-1 PF 0.93-1.30. Win rates are mostly 49-66%, with the average win about equal to the average loss (GBPCAD and EURNZD: 72-77% winners, losses 2-3x wins). Verdict: 'highly broker dependend and not very scalable'; version 6.0 'seems the author optimized' 2015.

scalpers.name: GerFX QuantFlow Scalper, formerly 'NY Close Scalper' (Exler Consulting GmbH / Paul Exler, MT4 51340, July 2020, 900 USD); sister EAs Density Scalper, NightWalker, DeltaWave
scalpers.window: 'Around the New York close time (16:00 - 18:00 New York time)'; 'QFS and DS also only trades exactly one hour before and one hour after swap time'. NightWalker and DeltaWave trade up to 6 h on some pairs. DST is handled internally; backtests run on Tick Data Suite at GMT+2 with US DST.
scalpers.pairs: EURUSD, GBPUSD, EURCHF, USDCHF, USDCAD, EURAUD, EURCAD. M5.
scalpers.entry: 'A mean reversion strategy around the close of the New York session', based on a price channel whose calculation is not disclosed. A wait between same-side entries, extended by 15 min after a losing hour.
scalpers.exit: Fixed stop loss on every position; TP not disclosed. On Density Scalper the SL can be cut to a fraction of normal 30/45/60 minutes after swap time ('a larger SL before the spread spike at swap time and a smaller SL afterwards').
scalpers.filters: Max spread (set per pair automatically). No trades before swap time on negative triple-swap days. A news filter (high impact, central-bank events, speeches) plus a 'breaking news' filter. A stock-market-crash filter (no trading if the S&P 500 fell more than a threshold over the last 8 h). A Christmas-New Year pause. A daily equity stop measured from 17:00 GMT. Caps on total positions and on positions per currency. The author also says to turn it off around elections.
scalpers.real_evidence: Signal 417005 has been deleted. Author's own statements: the maximum backtest drawdown is about 56 USD per 0.01 lot over 16 years, and it happened in 2008; 'flash crashes can cause big losses for night scalpers' (Jan 2019); spreads 'can go up to 20 pips after swap time'; Dukascopy's early-year spreads are 'like 10 pips on average on some symbols'. His backtests use 5 USD commission and a 150-250 ms delay.

scalpers.name: Black Night (Heiko Kendziorra, MT4 74678 / MT5 76078, Dec 2021)
scalpers.window: Broker clock GMT+2/+3 with rollover at 00:00 (= 17:00 NY). MT4: HourStart 22 and HourEnd 23, i.e. orders placed 15:00-16:00 NY. The vendor says it 'does not open trades in the difficult rollover hour' and 'starts trading one hour before the usual night scalping time to take profit without swap'. MT5: HourStart 22 to HourEnd 1 (15:00-18:00 NY), with low activity in the rollover hour.
scalpers.pairs: MT4: AUDCHF, CADCHF, EURCHF, GBPUSD, GBPCHF, GBPJPY, USDCHF, EURAUD, AUDCAD, CHFJPY, GBPCAD, plus AUDUSD, AUDJPY, EURGBP, EURCAD at half size. MT5: AUDCHF, AUDUSD, AUDJPY, EURUSD, GBPUSD, EURGBP, EURCHF, CHFJPY. M5.
scalpers.entry: The vendor: it 'uses like many night scalpers the Bollinger Bands indicator ... sets from a certain hour on limit orders at the external Bollinger Bands'. The limit order follows the band; buys and sells are handled independently.
scalpers.exit: A hidden TP when price is a set number of points past the middle Bollinger line ('the line in the middle triggers the take profit'), a wider visible TP2, and a hard SL. Internal per-pair presets shift the SL, TP and order distance.
scalpers.filters: MaxSpread deletes pending orders ('in the rollover hour usually all limit orders are deleted'). Filters on where price sits relative to previous days' and weeks' highs and lows. Correlated pairs are excluded once one trade is open. Lower activity on US holidays. No trading from late December to 2 January.
scalpers.real_evidence: All five advertised signals (1278063, 1280934, 1307592, 1318637, 2135693) have been deleted. The vendor writes that 'in the last week of Nov. 2021 ... many night scalpers had huge losses'. The EA is optimised for RoboForex ECN; with MetaQuotes demo tick data 'the shown test results double'; about half of the brokers' downloadable tick histories were corrupted.

scalpers.name: Keep Sleeping EA (Dmitry Homenkov, MT5 73548, Oct 2021)
scalpers.window: 'Usually from 22:00 to 3:00 GMT+2(+3)' server time, i.e. 15:00-20:00 NY. Orders are set at the start and removed at the end. Pause intervals, for example 23:45-00:10 (16:45-17:10 NY) or 23:50-00:15. Remaining positions are closed at a set time, for example 04:00 server (21:00 NY). Pending orders are removed at 23:30 server on Friday.
scalpers.pairs: GBPUSD, AUDCAD, EURAUD, EURCAD, GBPAUD, GBPCAD, GBPNZD, EURCHF, GBPCHF, USDCAD, EURGBP, USDCHF, AUDUSD, NZDUSD, EURNZD, CHFJPY. Works on M5 internally.

scalpers.exit: TP set by a 'take profit ratio' (0 = shortest target; about 30 points, i.e. 3 pips, on EURUSD on average). A trailing TP ('almost all losses are fixed by trailing TP without triggering main SL'). A 'safe SL' against spread widening. A forced close time.
scalpers.filters: Pause intervals around the rollover, pending orders removed before the weekend, a balance stop.
scalpers.real_evidence: None (no signal).

scalpers.name: Waiting Night MT5 (Marat Baiburin, MT5 77928, Feb 2022)
scalpers.window: 'Quiet hours' at night. The user enters the broker's winter GMT offset and DST. Hours are not published. There is an option to trade the Sunday-to-Monday night. All trades close within 3-5 hours.
scalpers.pairs: USDCAD, USDCHF, USDJPY, EURCAD, EURCHF, EURUSD, EURGBP, EURAUD, GBPUSD, CHFJPY, AUDCAD, AUDUSD.
scalpers.entry: Market or limit orders at a computed level ('Level calculation'), gated by a per-pair volatility filter ('Koef calculation', 'Force 1/2'). The logic is not disclosed.

scalpers.real_evidence: Signal 1738184 has been deleted. The vendor says the parameters were optimised on 10 years of Dukascopy data with floating spread and slippage.

scalpers.pairs: GBPUSD, GBPCAD, USDCAD, GBPAUD, EURAUD, EURCAD, EURGBP, GBPCHF, EURUSD, USDCHF, NZDUSD, EURNZD, USDJPY, EURCHF, AUDJPY, AUDNZD.

The vendor's blog speaks of 'capturing consistent mean reversion targets during rollover' and says that 'at exactly 00:00 server time (rollover) ... retail brokers ... widen their spreads, sometimes by 30 to 40 pips'. 00:00 server is 17:00 NY on a GMT+2/+3 clock.

scalpers.name: Night Walker EA (Ivan Pochta, MT5 160849, Jan 2026)
scalpers.window: 'The transition from the US session close to the Asian session open', so from around 17:00 NY. Exact hours are in the preset files, not on the page.

scalpers.name: Other Bollinger-channel night scalpers on MQL5 Market: Night horizontal (78039), BG Robonight (22635, 2017), Night Bollinger (24758), Synevir (27003, free, 2017)
scalpers.window: Night horizontal: 'at night, near the rollover', starting at 20-23 server for 1-6 hours. BG Robonight: 'at the junction of the American and Pacific sessions', on an Eastern European / NY-close terminal clock. Night Bollinger: times given in UTC+2, hours not published. Synevir: 00:05-08:00 server (17:05-01:00 NY on GMT+2/+3), closing everything at 23:59.
scalpers.pairs: Night horizontal: GBPUSD M5 by default. BG Robonight: AUDCAD, CADCHF, EURCAD, GBPCAD, AUDCHF, GBPAUD, M15. Night Bollinger: EURCHF, USDCHF, GBPCAD, M15. Synevir: EURUSD, USDJPY, M5.
scalpers.entry: Night horizontal: trades only when the Bollinger channel is horizontal, with pending orders at the channel edges. BG Robonight: enters a set delta beyond the outer Bollinger band, only when the channel width is between a minimum and a maximum. Night Bollinger: 'price breakout from Bollinger Bands', other details kept secret. Synevir: Bollinger plus Stochastic, RSI and a maximum gap to a fast moving average.

scalpers.filters: Max spread in all four (Night horizontal closes orders when the spread widens). BG Robonight has a news filter; Synevir has trade-day switches. Night horizontal and Synevir offer a one-step lot increase after a loss (martingale-like); BG Robonight has optional averaging.

research.consensus:
This consensus is built only from elements that several sources state. No vendor publishes its exact rule.

1) Clock. Trading happens in a short window tied to the New York close, 17:00 New York. Almost every vendor writes this as 00:00 on a broker clock set to GMT+2 in winter and GMT+3 in US summer.
- Most sources trade somewhere between about one hour before and three hours after the close (16:00-20:00 NY).
- The most cited core is the first hour after the rollover, 17:00-18:00 NY. Examples: the SFE review ('the hour directly after the rollover ... all pairs trade here'), MapleLeafs and MilkyWay (00:00-01:00 server), the free Night scalper bot (17:10-17:50 NY), NoCap ('during rollover') and signal 683917 ('around the rollover').
- Sources disagree about the rollover hour itself:
  - SFE treats it as the core hour.
  - Black Night and Evening Scalper Pro avoid it and trade before it.
  - GerFX / NY Close Scalper, Night Scalper EU and Night Swimmer straddle it (16:00-18:00 NY).
  - Keep Sleeping pauses from 16:45 to 17:10 NY.
  - Older Russian templates run all night on the European clock: article 1373 (20:00-10:00 server), article 4102 (22:00-08:00 UTC) and PolyFit (17:00-03:00 NY).
  - The AM2 Code Base EA stops trading at the close.
- Most sources do not trade Friday night and usually skip the Sunday open and holidays.

2) Instruments. The quiet crosses and dollar pairs, chiefly the EUR, GBP, CHF, CAD, AUD and NZD crosses: EURCHF, EURGBP, EURCAD, GBPCAD, EURAUD, AUDCAD, GBPCHF, CADCHF, AUDNZD, GBPAUD, EURNZD. Plus EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDCHF and USDCAD. JPY pairs are a minority (CHFJPY, USDJPY).

3) Entry: fade a short-term stretch inside a quiet channel. Sell at or above the upper edge; buy at or below the lower edge.
- The edge is most often an outer Bollinger band on M5 to M15 bars: the AM2 code, Zabudskiy, Black Night ('like many night scalpers'), Luna AI, BG Robonight, Night Walker, Night horizontal and Synevir.
- Other definitions of the edge:
  - the high/low of the bars just before the window (article 1373, Asia Balance);
  - a regression band (PolyFit);
  - symmetric buy-limit and sell-limit orders at a distance from price (Night Hunter Pro, NoCap, Keep Sleeping, Night Ranger, SFE).
- Many sources only enter when the channel is quiet:
  - a maximum band width (AM2);
  - a band width between a minimum and a maximum (BG Robonight; Night Hunter Pro's minimum range in % of ATR);
  - ADX neither too low nor too high (Night Walker);
  - a horizontal channel (Night horizontal);
  - a volatility cap (Night Swimmer, Waiting Night).
- No two sources use the same band settings: periods of 4-40 bars, 1-2 standard deviations, timeframes from M1 to H1. There is no common value, so the lab has to declare one.

4) Exit: a small target and a wider fixed stop, plus a time exit.
- The target is either the middle band / mean (Black Night, PolyFit, the GitHub and StockSharp versions) or a few pips (AM2 2-8, Keep Sleeping about 3, article 1373 1-5).
- The stop is fixed and several times the target: AM2 37-45 pips, PolyFit 45, Waiting Night 50-100. Only Zabudskiy's 14-pip stop against a 12-pip target is close to 1:1.
- The surviving live accounts win 68-89% of their trades, and their average loss equals 1.3 to 6.5 average wins.
- In lab terms (1 R = the stop distance), that means many wins of roughly 0.2-0.7 R against full 1 R losses. Before costs, roughly 60-85% winners are needed just to break even.
- The time exit closes the trade at a fixed hour: AM2 at the close; articles 4102 and 1373 and NoCap at the end of the window; Keep Sleeping at about 21:00 NY; Waiting Night after 3-5 h. Signal 683917 and Luna hold 1-4 h on average, but Night Hunter Pro and NightVision hold 11-15 h.

5) Filters.
- A maximum spread that blocks entries and cancels pending orders (almost all sources).
- Protection from the rollover minutes: a pause, deleting pending orders, or a wider or hidden stop through the spike.
- One position per pair, and often a cap on positions in the same currency.
- A news filter (many, not all).
- No trades before a negative triple swap (Wednesday).
- Christmas to New Year and US holidays off.

Simplest rule that captures what most share. This is a hypothesis built from the shared elements, not any vendor's code:
- Monday to Thursday nights, in New York time.
- A window after the 17:00 NY rollover, for example 17:00-20:00 NY, with no entries during the rollover minutes.
- On M5 bars of each pair: sell when a bar closes above the upper Bollinger band; buy when it closes below the lower band.
- Take profit at the middle band. Stop loss fixed and wider than the target.
- If neither is hit, close at market at a fixed hour the same night.
- Skip an entry when the spread is above a cap. One position per pair.

Points where the sources disagree belong in the declared single-parameter neighbours, not in the main rule:
- trading before, across or after the rollover;
- middle-band target or fixed-pip target, and whether the middle band is frozen at entry or follows price;
- band period, width and timeframe;
- stop size: fixed pips, or a multiple of band width or ATR;
- market or limit entry;
- one trade per side per night (article 1373, NoCap) or repeated entries.

A minority instead fades the whole US-session move or the distance from the session open (Newton's third law, ReturnToOpen).

cautions: Rollover spreads decide the result. Vendors report spreads of up to 20 pips after swap time (GerFX), 30-40 pips at 00:00 server (NoCap), and night spreads 1.5-2x normal on EURCHF, GBPCAD and EURCAD (article 1373). The only independent test says the strategy's core hour is the one right after the rollover, 'when the spreads are the highest'. The lab's FP cost frame scales Dukascopy's intraday spread shape but clips it at 6x, which can understate the first minutes after 17:00 NY. Either forbid entries in those minutes or cost them with unclipped real spreads, and report how many entries, stops and targets fall between 16:55 and 17:30 NY.

FP Markets' Raw spreads on crosses are not verified (as the lab already notes). For targets of a few pips they are the decisive input. Before believing any result, record FP's live bid/ask on the chosen crosses from about 16:30 to 21:00 NY over a few dozen nights; the lab's existing spread recorder can do this. Dukascopy's own spreads were very wide in early years (GerFX: about 10 pips on average on some symbols) and do not match FP's around the rollover.

Results depend on the broker and on trade size. Black Night: MetaQuotes demo data doubles the backtest result. Signal 683917: copy error of about 1 pip at 3x size, about 4 pips at 8x and 8-12 pips at 20x. Night Hunter Pro guide: slippage becomes significant above 0.5-1 lot per account. ForexBenchmark: 'highly broker dependend and not very scalable'. A 1,000 EUR account trading 0.01-0.1 lot is in the small-size range where these robots do best, but live slippage at 17:00-18:00 NY can still exceed the lab's 0.1-0.3 bp assumption.

Execution model. Most vendors leave limit orders resting at the band (no spread crossed, filled on touch). The lab fills at market at the next M1 open plus slippage. A market-fill test is conservative compared with the vendors; a limit-order simulation on M1 bars is optimistic unless it requires price to trade through the level. Declare one before running and do not switch after seeing results.

Payoff shape and costs. Small targets against wide stops give 68-89% winners, but each loss wipes out 1.3 to 6.5 wins; the surviving live accounts made PF 1.05 to 1.79. Costs are a large share of a few-pip target, so the bars of PF at least 1.12 after costs and at least 1.04 at costs x1.5 are demanding; report the result before costs as well. On M1 bars, many bars will touch both a nearby target and the stop; the lab's stop-first rule is conservative here, so report the share of such bars.

Night tail events lie inside 2013-2021 and must stay in the test: the SNB floor removal on 15 Jan 2015 (EURCHF and every CHF cross), the GBP flash crash on 7 Oct 2016 (Asian session), the JPY/AUD flash crash on 3 Jan 2019 (GerFX: 'flash crashes can cause big losses for night scalpers'), and the last week of Nov 2021 (Black Night: 'many night scalpers had huge losses'). Interventions are a further risk (article 1373). Dropping CHF pairs or these nights after seeing results would be selection.

Curve fitting is normal in this genre: hours set per pair (SFE's lists, PolyFit's minute-level schedule file), per-pair presets (AM2, Night Hunter Pro, Black Night, Luna), five free optimisation parameters (Waiting Night), and an author tuning a recent year (SFE v6 'optimized' 2015). The lab's test should use one window and one parameter set for all pairs, with single-parameter neighbours only, as in Addendum K.

Survivorship and changing regimes. Of the 26 signal links printed on night-scalper product pages, 22 no longer exist, and several products are delisted (Evening Scalper Pro, Night Owl, SFE Night Scalper, StarX). The survivors made PF 1.05-1.79 with drawdowns of 22-48%. Vendors themselves report bad periods: 2008 (GerFX); 2007-2008 (the 2008 '_rdb_' EURGBP Asian-session thread, mql5.com/en/forum/179042); 2022-2023 (Night Hunter Pro reviews, NightTradeEA's 'unsuccessful year 2023', Rollover Scalper's 'markets aren't that favorable'); and summer worse than winter, with targets shrinking (article 1373). Expect years with no edge; the bar of 60% of years positive will matter.

Clock and daylight saving. Vendors use a broker clock of GMT+2 in winter and GMT+3 in US summer, so that 00:00 = 17:00 New York. Windows quoted in GMT, Moscow time or UK time shift by one hour during the weeks of March and October-November when US and European DST differ. Define the window directly in New York time, as the lab already does, and do not convert vendor hours through a fixed GMT offset.

Swap. A position opened before 17:00 NY and held through it pays swap, triple on Wednesday. Vendors filter negative swaps (Night Hunter Pro, GerFX, Luna) or trade before the rollover to avoid it (Black Night). A window that opens after 17:00 NY and closes the same night avoids swap entirely; if the main window crosses 17:00 NY, swaps must be charged.

Correlation. The crosses share currencies (EUR, GBP, CAD, AUD, CHF, NZD) and move together on a dollar or risk shock. Vendors cap exposure to one currency (Night Hunter Pro 2, GerFX 2, Luna 3 correlated trades, per-currency limits in Black Night and Waiting Night). The lab's one-position-per-instrument rule does not cap this; at 7% risk per trade, several correlated stops in one night could cost 20-30% of the account. The t-statistic on daily sums and the 25% maximum share per instrument are the right protections; consider declaring a same-currency cap as part of the rule.

Information leakage. Several public records fall in the lab's validation and holdout years: the sbrakni GitHub repo (2022-2026 backtests), the NoCap signal (2026), Kartezhnikov's MT5 signal (2022 on), Luna's public record (2022 on) and product reviews after 2022. Their per-pair profit figures must not influence the basket. Keep the list of crosses fixed in dl_round6.py before this research and pick the basket by a rule declared without them.

Data quality at night. Article 4102 shows +152% on 'OHLC on M1' against +48% on real ticks for the same few-pip strategy, and Black Night found about half of brokers' tick histories corrupted. Before running, check each pair for missing or stale M1 bid/ask bars between 16:55 and 17:30 NY, and skip nights with gaps, as Addendum K's quote test did.

Target against spread. On very quiet nights the distance to the middle band can be smaller than the spread (article 1373 and Night horizontal warn that the spread can exceed the size of the swings). Some sources require a minimum channel width (BG Robonight, Night Hunter Pro's minimum range in % of ATR). A minimum distance from entry to target, as a multiple of the current spread, is supported by sources and could be one declared filter.

Sources I could not read. ForexFactory threads are behind a Cloudflare block (403 for both curl and WebFetch); I found none that were usable and relied on MQL5 forum threads instead. Myfxbook (SFE Night Scalper, Night Ranger) also returned 403. web.archive.org is blocked, so delisted product pages (Evening Scalper Pro, Night Owl) are known only from search-engine snippets. Night Hunter Pro's real hours sit behind its 'Smart Time Filter' and are not published.

designs.addendum_md:
## Addendum L (2026-11-14; written BEFORE any run): round 6 — night mean reversion on FX crosses (idea 2 of the MQL5 survey)
**Origin.** The survey of public MQL5 robots (`results/r2/mql5_survey.json`, idea 2) found one long live record of a
"night scalper": signal 683917 (ICMarkets, public since July 2020, PF 1.79, 70.5 % winners, average win 3.43 against
average loss 4.56 EUR, equity drop 38 %, rules not published). A second research pass (2026-11-14; about twenty public
sources: free code, articles, vendor manuals, live signals and one independent Dukascopy backtest; the list of sources
and quotes is kept with this declaration) extracted what most of these robots share. The rule below is that common core,
written as one computable rule with one parameter set for every cross. Where the sources disagree, the most common
choice is the main rule and the main alternatives are the neighbours. It replaces the survey's placeholder (M15 bars,
18:30–23:45, one trade a night, six crosses), which was written before the sources were read and was never declared.
Before this text, only the column headers of the price files (and one first row, to check the time unit) were opened;
no statistic was computed on any price.

**Frozen rule `night_fade` (the main configuration).**
- **Basket**: the twelve crosses fixed in `dl_round6.py` before this research: EURCAD, GBPCAD, EURAUD, AUDCAD, EURGBP,
  EURCHF, GBPCHF, AUDNZD, NZDCAD, CADCHF, GBPAUD, EURNZD. All twelve, none chosen on results. No major pair: the idea and
  its evidence are about crosses, the majors' hours were already studied in round 3 under the FP cost model, and the
  basket keeps one data source and one cost model. A cross leaves the basket only if its download cannot be completed,
  which would be reported before any run.
- **Data**: Dukascopy M1 bid and ask (`lab/data/raw_r6`), 2013–2021 only (no later file is on disk). Frames built like
  `prep_round3._merge` (inner join of bid and ask by minute, repeated flat bars and crossed bars dropped), trading days
  Monday–Friday by the 17:00 New York rule, read with the filter ts < 2022-01-01 and checked. Prices in each cross's
  quote currency; one pip = 0.0001 for all twelve.
- **Evenings** (New York wall clock, `America/New_York`; daylight saving from the tz database, so every time below keeps
  its place against the 17:00 New York rollover all year while its UTC time moves by one hour; the switches fall on
  Sundays, never traded): an evening E is a Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday from 2013-01-01 to 2021-12-30; it
  opens the trading day E+1. Skipped for the whole basket: E from 24 December to 1 January; E or E+1 a New York Stock
  Exchange full holiday (`idxus_lib.us_holidays`; the mourning closure of 2018-12-05 counts as a normal day). That leaves
  1,753 evenings (194–196 a year). Skipped for one cross: no M1 bar of that cross starting in [17:00, 17:15) on E (bars
  before the first decision only); warm-up not complete (fewer than 480 completed H1 bars at 17:15, or fewer than 20
  earlier reference evenings for the spread cap below; about the first five weeks of 2013).
- **Bars and bands**: M5 bars (the sources' most common bar) = `goldlab.data.bars(frame, "5min")` (UTC grid, which is
  also the New York 5-minute grid; labelled by start; an empty 5-minute bucket has no bar), on mid prices ((bid + ask) / 2,
  the same in every cost scenario). For bar j: middle = mean of the mid closes of bar j and the 19 bars before it; σ =
  their population standard deviation (divide by 20); upper = middle + 2.0 σ; lower = middle − 2.0 σ (the indicator's
  standard settings: no two sources use the same ones). Bar j is usable only if bar j−19 starts at most 120 minutes
  before bar j ends.
- **Signal**: the decision times are the ends of the 5-minute buckets from 17:15 to 19:55 New York on E (33 a night;
  most sources trade from the rollover to about 20:00 New York, and the first quarter hour after 17:00, when spreads
  jump, is left out); the M5 bar of the bucket that ends then, if it exists, is the signal bar. Buy if its mid close is
  below the lower band; sell if it is above the upper band.
- **Spread cap** (the filter almost every source uses): the signal is dropped if the spread at the signal bar's close
  (ask close − bid close of its last M1 bar, base cost frame) is above 2.0 × the cross's normal night spread, which
  blocks rollover tails and spikes but not normal nights. Normal night spread for E = the median, over the 20 most recent
  earlier reference evenings of that cross (evenings that pass the calendar and that cross's quote test and have at least
  one of its M1 bars in [17:15, 21:00)), of each evening's median spread over its M1 bars in [17:15, 21:00).
- **Entry**: at market at the open of the first M1 bar starting at or after the decision time; dropped if that bar
  starts more than 5 minutes late. A buy fills at the ask open + 0.1 bp, a sell at the bid open − 0.1 bp. Also dropped
  if that open has already reached the target (buy: ask open ≥ target; sell: bid open ≤ target), because the trade
  server would refuse a take-profit on the wrong side of the price.
- **Exits**: *target* (the sources' most common) = the middle band of the signal bar, frozen as a price level, a
  resting take-profit: a long exits when a bar's bid high reaches it, a short when a bar's ask low does; filled at the
  level, or better on a gap; no slippage. *Stop* = 2.0 × the mean (mid high − mid low) of the 480 most recent completed
  H1 bars at the decision time (`bars(frame, "1h")`; completed = bar start + 60 minutes ≤ decision time; the measure of
  Addendum K), set from the fill and fixed: a scale-free reading of the sources' wide fixed stops (37–60 pips, several
  times the target); checked on the bid low for longs and the ask high for shorts, filled at the stop or worse on a gap,
  with 0.3 bp of slippage. When stop and target are both touched in one M1 bar, the stop comes first. *Time exit*: at
  market at the open of the first M1 bar at or after 21:00 New York, one hour after the last entry, as Keep Sleeping
  closes (`exit_index`: if that bar starts more than 30 minutes late, the open of the last bar before the gap), with
  0.1 bp of slippage. No trade is held overnight.
- **Positions**: one per cross. A signal that comes while the cross has an open trade (entry bar at or before that
  trade's exit bar) is ignored: no queue, no reversal, no adding. Later signals of the same evening can be taken, on
  either side. There is no limit on the number of crosses open together and no cap per currency (both are reported).
- **Results in R**: R = side × (exit fill − entry fill) / |entry fill − stop|; fills include spread, commission and
  slippage.

**Costs.**
- **Base model**: Dukascopy's own minute bid and ask, unclipped, plus FP Markets' Raw commission. Why not an FP spread
  model: FP's Raw spreads on crosses are not verified, so an FP model would rest on an invented level, and its clip of
  the intraday shape at 6 × the daily median would understate the minutes after 17:00, which matter most here.
  Dukascopy's quotes are a real ECN's night spreads, rollover tails included, and carry no commission (Dukascopy charges
  its own separately), so adding FP's commission counts nothing twice.
- **Commission**: 6 USD per 100,000 units of base per round trip, folded into the quotes (bid − c/2, ask + c/2, with c
  in bp of each bar's mid), at fixed values of one unit of base: EUR 1.18, GBP 1.40, AUD 0.78, NZD 0.72, CAD 0.80 USD
  (round values near the 2013–2021 averages, fixed here, not measured on lab data). So c = 0.508 bp for the five EUR
  crosses, 0.429 bp for the three GBP crosses, 0.769 bp for AUDCAD and AUDNZD, 0.833 bp for NZDCAD and 0.750 bp for
  CADCHF.
- **Slippage**: 0.1 bp on market fills, 0.3 bp on stops (the lab's FX values).
- **No swap**: every trade opens at or after 17:15 and closes by 21:30 New York at the latest, the same evening, so it
  never crosses a 17:00 New York rollover; the engine's swap is checked to be zero on every trade.
- **Costs × 1.5**: the base frame's spread (Dukascopy spread + commission) × 1.5 around the mid, slippage × 1.5.
  **Gross** (information): mid quotes, no slippage.
- Every decision (signals, spread cap, entry delay, refused take-profit, target, stop distance) is computed once on the
  base frame; the costs × 1.5 and gross runs replay the same orders on other quotes.
- Known biases, said now: Dukascopy's cross spreads were wider in 2013–2015 than ECN spreads are today (harder early
  years), and they may be wider or narrower than FP's at night today (unknown until FP's spreads are read).

**Neighbours (the budget, all logged; each changes one thing from the main).** (1) `first_hour`: decision times
17:15–17:55 only (the hour after the rollover that the only independent test calls the core). (2) `moving_mid`: the
same entries, no resting target; exit at market at the open of the first M1 bar at or after the end of the first M5 bar
that ends after the entry and whose mid close is at or beyond its own middle band (long: ≥; short: ≤); stop and 21:00
exit unchanged. (3) `width_2.5`: bands at ± 2.5 σ. (4) `m15`: bands and signals on M15 bars (20 bars = 300 minutes;
usable if bar j−19 starts at most 360 minutes before bar j ends), decision times at the ends of the 15-minute buckets
from 17:15 to 19:45. (5) `stop_3.0`: stop = 3.0 × the mean H1 range. (6) `one_per_night`: at most one trade per cross
per evening (its first signal that passes every filter). Seven configurations with the main.

**In sample only (2013–2021), frames cut while read. The verdict is read on the main only.** Pass = all of the
PROTOCOL_V3 section 4 basket bars, with the other PROTOCOL_V2 bars kept as in Addenda B and K: n ≥ 250; pooled PF ≥ 1.12;
t on daily sums of R ≥ 2.5 (by trading day of entry, days with at least one trade); ≥ 60 % of calendar years positive
(at least 6 of 9); pooled PF ≥ 1.04 at costs × 1.5; at least 65 % of the crosses with a positive expectancy (8 of 12);
no cross above 25 % of the pooled profit (a pooled total ≤ 0 fails); median pooled PF of the six neighbours ≥ 1.06;
pooled every-signal expectancy > 0; hold ≤ 5 trading days; pooled null ≥ 97.5th percentile; |weekly correlation with the
sum of the ten| ≤ 0.30.
- **Null** (section 4: same clock time, random day, same instrument): 200 replays, numpy `default_rng(0)`. Each filled
  trade of the main is re-entered on the same cross, on an evening drawn at random among that cross's tradable evenings
  (calendar, quote test and warm-up passed), at the open of the first M1 bar at or after the clock time of its own entry
  bar (another evening is drawn if that bar is more than 5 minutes late, at most 20 draws, then the replay is dropped and
  counted), with the same side, the same stop and target distances as fractions of the entry price, the time exit at
  21:00 New York of that evening, base costs and one position per cross. Statistic: the mean R of all replayed trades of
  the twelve crosses together; percentile = share of the 200 replays strictly below the main's pooled mean R.
- **Correlation**: Addendum K's convention: the ten's official trades read with entry_time < 2022-01-01 in the read,
  exits in 2022 dropped; weekly sums of R by exit week (W-SUN, UTC); every week from 2014-01-01 to 2021-12-31 counted
  (418 weeks, an empty week = 0); Pearson between the main's pooled weekly R and the sum of the ten.
- **Reported, not judged.** For every configuration, pooled and per cross: n, PF, t on daily sums and on trades,
  expectancy, total R, R by year, long and short apart, win rate, average win and average loss in R and their ratio
  (signal 683917: 70.5 % winners, average win / average loss = 0.75), exits by target / stop / time, hold, net and
  gross bp per trade, cost per trade in bp, target and stop distances in pips, and the same at costs × 1.5 and gross.
  For the main also: entries by New York hour, by weekday and by daylight-saving regime; signals dropped by each filter;
  evenings skipped by reason and cross; entries, stop exits and target exits between 16:55 and 17:30; the share of
  trades whose stop and target fell in one M1 bar; trades whose costs × 1.5 fill was already past the target; expectancy
  by the ratio of target distance to spread at the signal (< 1, 1–2, 2–3, ≥ 3; information, never a filter); winning
  days, weeks and months; worst evening, worst week, maximum drawdown in R; the number of crosses open at once and the
  most open trades on one currency and side; the account check at 7 % of 1,000 EUR (lots against the 0.01 minimum,
  margin at 1:500); and the evenings of 2016-10-06 (pound flash crash, around 19:07 New York) and 2019-01-02 (yen and
  Australian-dollar flash crash, around 17:40 New York), which fall inside the window and stay in the test.
- **Bookkeeping**: one line per configuration and cross plus one pooled line per configuration (84 + 7) in
  `results/r2/round6/night_fade/trials.jsonl`, whatever the result; the readings of any detail left open go into
  `declared.json`, with its sha256, before any return is computed. A pass is attacked by an independent
  re-implementation before anything else. A kept rule gets ONE look at 2022–2025, declared separately; the 2022–2025
  files of these crosses are downloaded only after that declaration. Before any real use, FP's night spreads on the
  crosses are read with `ReleveFP` (`lab/live_ai/mql5/ReleveFP.mq5`, InpSymbols = the crosses, InpDays = 30, about 20
  Monday–Thursday nights; the commission from a demo round trip), the result is recomputed with them under a rule
  declared then, and the demo account comes first. The 2026 holdout stays untouched.

**Said before the run.** The vendors' records are better than this test can be: they rest limit orders at the band (no
spread paid to enter), tune per pair, trade at low-spread ECN brokers, and are survivors (22 of the 26 signal links on
their pages no longer exist). The lab enters at market and pays the whole spread on every trade. Small night moves may
well partly come back (liquidity providers widen their quotes and absorb small pushes), but that is the liquidity
provider's side of the spread, and the lab's FX gross edges so far were 1–2 bp at best. Arithmetic, from the rule alone:
a win earns the distance from the fill to the middle band, and the mid must travel that distance plus one full spread;
with bands of 2 σ of twenty 5-minute closes this distance is a few pips at night, against an all-in cost of roughly
1.5–3 pips (Dukascopy night spread, 0.4–0.8 bp of commission, slippage); with a stop of twice the mean hourly range, a
win is of the order of +0.1 to +0.3 R and a loss up to −1 R. PF ≥ 1.12 needs a net mean of about 6 % of the mean
absolute result per trade, and PF ≥ 1.04 at costs × 1.5 needs the gross reversion to exceed about 1.5 times the base
cost. Expected: of the order of 15,000–45,000 trades; 55–70 % winners; a gross PF above 1 but a net PF below 1.12,
failing on costs (PF, costs × 1.5, years). The null can pass even then: it tests the timing, not whether costs are
covered. Prior of a pass in sample about 5 %; of a later 2022–2025 pass about 2 %. If it passed, it would add a small
independent sleeve (expected |ρ| with the ten below 0.1), not a multiplier; at 7 % risk per trade, a dozen crosses open
on the same evening would need a per-evening risk budget, declared separately before any real use.

risks: Costs decide the verdict, and the spread input is uncertain. Dukascopy's night spreads on crosses are not FP's. If they are wider (as is likely for 2013-2015), the test can give a false negative. If they are narrower than FP's spreads at 17:15-21:00 New York, it can give a false positive. Only ReleveFP readings can settle this, and they come after the run.
Market entries (the lab convention) pay a full spread that the vendors' resting limit orders avoid. A fail therefore does not refute the limit-order version, and that version is not tested.

The spread cap (2 x the normal night spread) may block a large share of the signals or almost none. Its effect is unknown until the precheck and is reported. It cannot be changed after this declaration.

Tail events inside the window stay in the test: the GBP flash crash (2016-10-06, around 19:07 New York) and the JPY/AUD crash (2019-01-02, around 17:40 New York). Stops that gap through can give single trades of -5 to -20 R and decide the years-positive bar.

Correlated exposure: up to twelve crosses can be open in the same evening, sharing EUR, GBP, AUD, NZD, CAD and CHF. At 7 % risk per trade a bad evening could cost a large part of a 1,000 EUR account, and the margin at 1:500 could bind. The daily-sum t-statistic handles the inference, not the account risk. A per-evening risk budget would have to be declared before any real use.

There is no news filter. NZ and Australian releases (and, before 2015, RBNZ decisions near 17:00 New York) fall inside or near the window, so the test can lose on trades that vendors with news filters would skip.
The holiday calendar is NYSE-based. FX-specific thin days are traded: Easter Monday, Japanese and Australian holidays, and the Jan 2-3 evenings after New Year.
EURCHF in 2013 to January 2015, under the SNB floor, has very narrow bands, so its trades are mostly cost. It is kept by design and may drag the per-cross and per-year bars.

Daylight saving: in US winter the Tokyo open (19:00 New York) falls inside the entry window; in summer it is at 20:00. The two regimes may behave differently. This is only reported, never used to pick.

Thin crosses (NZDCAD, CADCHF, AUDNZD, EURNZD) may have missing minutes, stale quotes or bad ticks around the rollover. The data guards (quote test, band span, 5-minute entry delay) may drop many signals; bad ticks can create spurious stop or target fills.
Two neighbours (first_hour, one_per_night) are near-subsets of the main's trades and share its fate. The neighbours' median PF bar is therefore less independent than it looks.

The R scale: stops are normalised by the 24-hour mean H1 range, so target wins are small in R (about 0.1-0.3). PF on R depends on the stop-to-target ratio; stop_3.0 shows this sensitivity, and no other stop is allowed.

Multiple testing and survivorship: 7 configurations on top of thousands of earlier lab trials. The rule reconstructs hidden vendor logic from survivors, so even a pass is weaker evidence than it reads.
Regime risk: vendors report losses after 2022. The single 2022-2025 look, if it ever happens, may fail even after an in-sample pass.

Data completeness: five crosses (audnzd, nzdcad, cadchf, gbpaud, eurnzd) were still downloading when this was written, and gbpchf was partly done. A download that cannot be completed would change the basket without anyone choosing it; that must be reported before any run.

Implementation risk: this design cannot use the lab's r2.run / r2.evaluate (they rebuild orders on the stressed frame, and r2.costs has no entries for the crosses). ## Addendum L (2026-11-14; written BEFORE any run): round 6 — night mean reversion on currency pairs of Europe and North America
The user asked to go on with the tests ("continue les tests pour améliorer"). This round tests the second idea of the
MQL5 survey (`results/r2/mql5_survey.json`, `ideas_to_test` rank 2): the "night scalpers" that fade small stretches
after the New York close. Its best evidence is the signal 'Scalp IC Markets ECN'
(https://www.mql5.com/en/signals/683917): a real account public since July 2020, PF 1.79, 70.5 % winners, average loss
1.33 average wins, average hold 2 hours, rules not published. A review of the public night scalpers (robots, articles,
open code, one independent tick test; notes of 2026-11-14 in the session's scratch folder,
`round6_design/night_scalper_sources.md`; no price read) found no published rule, only shared elements: a short window
after the 17:00 New York rollover, quiet pairs, a fade of a close beyond an outer Bollinger band on M5 to M15 bars, a
target at the middle band with a wider fixed stop, a forced exit the same night and a maximum-spread filter. The rule
below is our canonical form of those elements, with as few numbers as we could, each fixed by a stated principle;
where the sources disagree, the alternatives are the neighbours. Frozen now: of the new data only file headers were
opened (format check) and nothing was computed on any price. As in round 5, every reading of a detail this text leaves
open goes into `declared.json`, with its sha256, before any return is computed.
**Basket: ten pairs, fixed by one principle.** Every pair formed from the five currencies whose home markets are all
shut during the New York evening: EUR, GBP, CHF, CAD and USD. The premise of night mean reversion is that with no home
market open, a stretch is mostly a liquidity imbalance that dealers lean against, not news. The main releases of all
five come out in their own mornings; only minor UK surveys appear at 00:01 London (about 19:01 New York).
- Pairs: EURGBP, EURCHF, EURCAD, GBPCHF, GBPCAD, CADCHF (Dukascopy M1 bid and ask, `data/raw_r6`, 2013–2021, from the
  list fixed in `dl_round6.py`) and EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDCHF, USDCAD (Dukascopy M1 bid and ask already in the lab,
  `data/r3/<pair>_m1.parquet`, read with the filter ts < 2022-01-01 inside the read call).
- Left out: the six AUD and NZD crosses of the download list (EURAUD, AUDCAD, AUDNZD, NZDCAD, GBPAUD, EURNZD). Sydney
  and Wellington are in session during the window and publish in it: Australian data at 19:30 New York in US winter,
  New Zealand data at 18:45 in US summer, RBNZ decisions at 20:00–22:00. JPY pairs are out for the same reason (Tokyo
  opens at 19:00 or 20:00 New York).
- Why the four dollar pairs: the same principle admits them (New York is shut), the sources name them, and the basket
  bars need the breadth. With six pairs, a real and even effect at the pass boundary (t = 2.5 on daily sums) would
  pass "no pair above 25 % of the profit" only about 6 % of the time; with ten, about 31 %, and 59 % at t = 3.5
  (synthetic arithmetic with independent pairs; no price data).
- No pair is chosen or dropped by hand, and no vendor's per-pair result was used.
**Evenings.** New York calendar dates E (America/New_York, tz database) from Monday to Thursday; the evening of E
opens the trading day E+1 (Tuesday to Friday, the lab's 17:00 New York day). Skipped: Friday and Saturday (closed),
Sunday (the weekly reopen: weekend gaps and the widest spreads), and every E from 24 December to 1 January (year-end:
thin markets and short broker hours; most sources pause then). Candidate evenings 2013-01-02 to 2021-12-23, about
1,830 per pair. No other calendar, news or volatility filter.
**Clock.** Signal bars are the M5 bars that close from 18:05 to 21:00 New York (36 bars).
- Why 18:00: the hour from 17:00 is the rollover, when spreads jump and CME's currency futures are shut (they reopen
  at 18:00 New York). Every position of the main opens at 18:05 New York or later and is closed by about 22:45, so the
  rollover spreads, which the lab cannot verify for FP, never enter the main result.
- Why three hours: the length of the window most sources trade after the close (17:00–20:00 New York), started after
  the rollover hour.
- All times are New York wall time, so the window follows the rollover through the daylight-saving changes.
**Bars and band, on mid prices.**
- M1 frames: Dukascopy bid and ask merged exactly as `prep_round3.py` builds `data/r3` (inner join on the minute,
  stale flat minutes and crossed quotes dropped, weekend trading days dropped).
- M5 bars on the clock grid. A bar exists if at least one M1 bar falls in it; its close is the mid of the last M1
  bar's bid and ask closes. Decision time: the bar's end.
- Band at the close of bar t, over the 20 most recent existing M5 bars, t included: middle μ = mean of the 20 closes;
  σ = their population standard deviation (divide by 20: Bollinger's definition and MT5's iBands); upper μ + 2σ, lower
  μ − 2σ. Fewer than 20 bars: no signal.
- Why these numbers: Bollinger's own defaults (20 bars, 2 σ) and the M5 bar, the most common among the sources,
  because no two sources agree. Why mid: so that a widening spread cannot create a signal by itself.
**Signal, cost filter and the night's one trade.**
- Close above the upper band: sell. Close below the lower band: buy (strict inequalities). D = |close − μ|, the
  distance to the target (always more than 2σ).
- Cost filter: the signal counts only if D ≥ 2 × C, where C = ask − bid at the close of the signal bar's last M1 bar,
  in the cost frame of the run (Dukascopy spread plus commission). The round-trip cost known at the decision may take
  at most half of the distance to the target. This is the scale-free form of the maximum-spread filter that almost
  every source uses, with one number for every pair; it also puts the stop (2D) at least four spreads away.
- One trade per pair per evening: the first signal bar of the window that passes the filter and has an entry bar gives
  the night's trade; later signals of that pair that evening are ignored. A second entry the same night is more often
  a trend (MQL5 article 1373), and one trade per evening keeps the evenings independent. No cap across pairs.
**Entry.** Market order at the open of the first M1 bar that starts at or after the signal bar's close; dropped if
that bar starts more than 5 minutes later (and a later signal of the evening may then give the trade). A buy fills at
the ask, a sell at the bid, plus 0.1 bp of slippage.
**Exits.** Orders are held from the fill and checked on M1 bid/ask highs and lows by the lab's simulator
(`goldlab.sim`); when stop and target are both touched in one bar, the stop comes first.
- Target: the signal bar's middle band μ, frozen; a fixed take-profit held at the broker, as the live signal does. It
  is a limit: a buy exits when the bid reaches it, a sell when the ask does; no slippage.
- Stop: 2 × D from the fill, so 1 R = 2D. The stop is wider than the target, as in every source that states both, here
  at the smallest whole multiple; one stop then costs two target wins. This is close to the realised shape of the
  surviving live night signals: in six of the seven records read, the average loss is 1.3 to 2.1 average wins (6.5 in
  the seventh). Those records lie mostly after 2021, so they serve only as a cross-check, never to set a number.
  Filled at the stop, or at a worse open, minus 0.3 bp.
- Time: at market at the open of the first M1 bar at or after entry + 100 minutes. That is 20 M5 bars: by then the
  band has renewed entirely and the frozen target belongs to a window that no longer overlaps it. If that bar is more
  than 30 minutes late, the exit is at the last bar before the gap (`exit_index`). The last time exit of the main
  falls at 22:45 New York (later only after missing minutes).
- No trailing, no break-even, no partial exit. Result of a trade in R: (exit fill − entry fill) × side / 2D, with the
  costs inside the fills.
**Costs. Primary model: real night quotes.**
- Quotes: Dukascopy's own minute bid and ask, unclipped, so each night carries its real widening.
- Commission: FP Markets Raw, 6 USD per lot of 100,000 units of base, round trip, folded into the quotes (half on each
  side of every M1 bar). In price per unit of base: EURUSD and GBPUSD 0.00006 exactly; USDCHF and USDCAD 0.6 bp of
  price exactly. Crosses at a fixed declared dollar value of the base: EUR 1.05, GBP 1.20, CAD 0.70 USD (round values
  near the low end of each currency's 2013–2021 range, from general knowledge, not measured, so the commission is if
  anything overstated). That gives 0.571 bp of price for EURGBP, EURCHF and EURCAD, 0.500 bp for GBPCHF and GBPCAD,
  and 0.857 bp for CADCHF.
- Slippage: 0.1 bp on market orders and 0.3 bp on stops (the lab's FX values), none on targets.
- Swap: none. Every position opens after 18:00 New York and is closed the same evening, long before the next 17:00
  rollover (asserted).
- Why not an FP spread model: FP's spreads on these crosses are not verified. The lab's FP model (today's spread with
  Dukascopy's intraday shape, clipped at 6×) can understate night and early-year costs. Real quotes also let the
  filter read the spread of the moment, as the robot would.
- Costs × 1.5, and both readings must pass: (a) the lab's stress, i.e. spread × 1.5 around the mid and slippage × 1.5,
  with orders rebuilt on the widened quotes (the filter then sees 1.5 C); (b) the same trades as the base run,
  re-simulated on those quotes.
- Gross: the same trades as the base run, on mid prices with no cost (information).
- Information only, never a verdict: the four dollar pairs also run on the lab's FP frames (`data/fp`, read with the
  filter), to show how far the two cost models differ where an FP figure exists.
**Configurations: 7, all logged in `results/r2/round6/night_fx/trials.jsonl`.**
- (1) The main, as above.
- Single-parameter neighbours: (2) window from 17:00 (signal bars 17:05–20:00: the sources' most common window,
  reaching into the rollover hour, priced with Dukascopy's real spreads and the same filter) and (3) from 19:00
  (19:05–22:00); (4) band at 1.5 σ and (5) at 2.5 σ; (6) stop at 1.5 × D and (7) at 3 × D.
- Everything else as in the main. The verdict is read on (1) only; (2) to (7) give the neighbours' median.
**In sample only.** 2013–2021, frames cut while read: the crosses' raw files hold 2013–2021 only and their frames are
asserted to end before 2022-01-01; the dollar pairs are read with ts < 2022-01-01 inside the read call.
`goldlab.r2.load` is never used (it reads whole files). `results/val_access.log` stays unchanged. No 2022–2025 file is
read or downloaded. 2026 untouched.
**Pass: the main must meet all twelve bars.** These are PROTOCOL_V3 section 4's basket bars, plus the single-sleeve
bars they do not replace, plus round 5's correlation bar.
- n ≥ 250.
- t on daily sums of R ≥ 2.5 (sum of the pairs' R per trading day of entry, over days with a trade).
- Pooled PF ≥ 1.12.
- Pooled PF ≥ 1.04 at costs × 1.5, in both readings.
- At least 6 of the 9 calendar years positive (by year of entry).
- At least 7 of the 10 pairs with positive expectancy (a pair with no trade counts as not positive).
- No pair above 25 % of the pooled net R (fails if that total is not positive).
- Neighbours' median pooled PF ≥ 1.06.
- Every-signal expectancy > 0. Here every signal bar of the window that passes the filter and has an entry bar is its
  own trade, overlaps allowed: stricter than the one-trade rule.
- Hold ≤ 5 trading days.
- Null at or above the 97.5th percentile.
- |weekly correlation with the sum of the ten| ≤ 0.30.
- If the pre-check drops a pair, the pair bars apply to the pairs kept.
**Null, on the pooled trades.** Each trade of the main is replayed 200 times on the same pair, at the same New York
minute of entry, on an evening drawn at random (uniform, with replacement, `numpy.random.default_rng(20261114)`) among
that pair's candidate evenings with an M1 bar at that minute. Each replay keeps the trade's side, its stop and target
distances as fractions of price, and the 100-minute time exit; base costs; every replay is simulated (no one-position
skip). Statistic: the pooled mean R. Percentile: the share of the 200 replay means strictly below the main's.
**Correlation.** As in round 5. The official trades of the ten are read with entry_time < 2022-01-01 and exits in 2022
are dropped. Weekly sums of R by exit week (W-SUN, UTC), every week from 2014-01-01 to 2021-12-31 (418 weeks). Pearson
with the sum of the ten; also reported with each cluster and each sleeve.
**Before the run (not trials).**
- A pre-check that reads quotes but computes no return. It covers: the frames (rows, stale and crossed minutes
  dropped, first and last bar); evenings per pair and year; coverage (a pair with an M1 bar in 18:00–21:00 New York on
  fewer than 90 % of its candidate evenings is dropped before the run); the quoted spread and all-in cost per pair and
  year at 18:00–21:00 and at 16:55–17:30 New York; the commission in pips; and the window in UTC across the
  daylight-saving switches.
- A synthetic test with known band crossings, fills, targets, stops and time exits.
- A truncation test: the decision quantities of at least 50 decisions per pair, recomputed on frames cut just after
  the signal bar, must equal the full-frame ones.
- A hand check, from the raw quotes, of five trades of the main: the first of 2013, 2015, 2017, 2019 and 2021.
**Reported, not judged.**
- For every configuration: n, PF, expectancy and t on daily sums; by pair, by year, long and short; net and gross bp;
  exit reasons (target, stop, time).
- Also for every configuration: the win rate with the average win and average loss in R. These are set against 683917
  (70.5 % winners, average loss 1.33 average wins), Night Hunter Pro (67.9 %, 1.8) and NightVision (67.6–68.8 %,
  1.8–2.1).
- Also for every configuration: the entries, stops and targets between 16:55 and 17:30 New York (none by construction,
  except in (2)).
- For the main, cost readings: costs × 1.5 in both readings, and gross, by pair and year; D/σ and D/C at entry; the
  spread paid.
- For the main, timing and outcomes: entries by half hour; trades that touch stop and target in the same minute;
  trades whose fill was already beyond the target; the share of evenings with a trade.
- For the main, breakdowns: crosses against dollar pairs; the result by currency, by weekday evening and by
  daylight-saving regime.
- For the main, risk: the worst trading days and the most positions open at once.
- For the main, named stress periods: the GBP flash-crash evening (2016-10-06, about 19:07 New York, inside the
  window), the week of 2021-11-22, and EURCHF before the floor ended (2015-01-15).
- For the main, the break-even all-in cost: the extra cost per round trip that would bring the pooled expectancy to
  zero on the same trades. It becomes the yardstick for FP's real spreads.
- For the main: the four dollar pairs on FP frames.
**After the run.**
- A fail is final. No other window, band, stop, filter, bar size or pair list is tried on these data. The AUD and NZD
  crosses, or the rollover hour, would be new ideas with their own declaration; the rollover hour would also need FP's
  real rollover spreads first.
- A pass is attacked by an independent re-implementation (own frames from the raw files, own band, own simulator;
  compared trade for trade). The attack also checks execution on the 1,000 EUR account: 0.01-lot steps, margin at
  1:500, how many of the ten can be open at once, and the worst night at 7 % risk per trade.
- A confirmed pass gets ONE look at 2022–2025, declared separately and committed before the 2022–2025 files of the six
  crosses are downloaded (only then). The 2022–2025 rows of the four dollar pairs, already on disk, are read only by
  that look.
- Before any real use: FP's night quotes on the ten pairs are read with ReleveFP (InpSymbols = the ten; InpDays = 60,
  or two runs a month apart, so that at least 30 Monday–Thursday evenings are covered), and the commission is read
  from a demo round trip. A pair whose FP median all-in cost over 18:00–21:05 New York is above 1.5 × the frame's
  median at the same minutes over 2019–2021 is not traded: it would lie outside the stress the rule passed. With fewer
  than seven pairs left, the rule is not used. Then the demo account first, never straight to real money.
**Said before the run.**
- Payoff arithmetic. At the filter's limit (D = 2C), a target hit nets (D − C/2) / 2D = 0.375 R and a stop costs 1 R.
  To break even, 73 % of target-or-stop outcomes must be targets, against about 55 % by chance (a random walk, with
  the half-spreads moving both triggers). At D = 4C it is 70 % against 61 %; with no cost, 67 % against 67 %.
- With no edge, the expected result is minus the round-trip cost: from −0.25 R at the limit to about −0.1 R. The night
  reversion must therefore add roughly 9 to 18 points of target hits beyond chance.
- The live night signals report 68–73 % winners, at brokers whose spreads on these crosses are probably tighter than
  Dukascopy's past ones. Dukascopy's were probably much wider in 2013–2015, so the early years should be the weakest.
- The lab's FX record: no FX rule is among the ten. The month-end fix (Addendum B) passed in sample and failed its
  2022–2025 look; round 3's other FX edges were 1–2 bp gross on the majors; round 4's weekend fade had none.
- For: a real six-year account, and an independent tick test of a commercial night scalper (PF 1.1–1.6 on most pairs,
  2010–2019). Both are centred on the rollover hour that this rule leaves out.
- Against: costs; our form is not any vendor's tuned rule; survivorship (22 of 26 signal links on night-scalper
  product pages are gone); and a demanding concentration bar.
- Our estimate: about one chance in eight of an in-sample pass, and one in 25 to 30 of reaching real use. Expected
  weekly correlation with the ten: about zero. Expected size: several thousand trades (at most one per pair per
  evening, about 18,300 pair-evenings).
- If it passes, it is a small sleeve on a market and a clock the ten never touch, not a multiplier of gains. At the
  robot's 7 % per trade, a night with several correlated stops among ten pairs could cost a large part of the account.
  Its risk would then have to be split across the night's positions; that is decided only after a pass.

designs.rationale:
This is the simplest form of the night-scalper family that the evidence supports. Each number is fixed by a stated principle, and no price data was touched: one raw header line was read for the format, and the only computation was a synthetic arithmetic check.

(1) Basket. All ten pairs (every pair of five currencies) of EUR, GBP, CHF, CAD and USD, whose home markets are shut and publish nothing major during the New York evening. No pair is picked by hand and no vendor's per-pair result is used. The six AUD/NZD crosses are left out because Sydney and Wellington publish inside the window. The four dollar pairs are added for two reasons: the same principle admits them, and with only six pairs the 25 % concentration bar is nearly unpassable even for a real effect (synthetic: about 6 % chance at t = 2.5, against 31 % with ten).

(2) Clock. Signal bars close from 18:05 to 21:00 New York. The window opens when the rollover hour ends and CME currency futures reopen, so FP's unverifiable rollover spreads never enter the main result. Three hours is the common window length in the sources.

(3) Signal. Bollinger(20, 2) on M5 mid closes, with the population standard deviation: the most common bar and the indicator's own defaults, because the sources disagree. Mid prices mean a spread spike cannot create a signal.

(4) Exits. Target: the middle band, frozen at the decision (a take-profit held at the broker, as the live signal does). Stop: 2 × D, the smallest whole multiple wider than the target. Time exit after 20 bars, when the band has fully renewed.

(5) One trade per pair per evening.

(6) Cost filter: D ≥ 2C, so the round-trip cost known at the decision takes at most half of the distance to the target. It is a scale-free maximum-spread filter.

(7) Costs. Dukascopy's real minute quotes, unclipped, plus the FP commission folded into the quotes. The commission is exact for the dollar pairs; for the crosses it uses fixed conservative dollar values of the base. Slippage 0.1 bp on market orders and 0.3 bp on stops. No swap, by construction. Because the filter depends on cost, the ×1.5 stress must pass in two readings: orders rebuilt, and same trades. FP's cross spreads are checked later with ReleveFP against the break-even cost.

(8) Neighbours. Three symmetric pairs on the most disputed numbers: window start ±1 h, band width ±0.5, stop 1.5 D / 3 D.

(9) Bars. The PROTOCOL_V3 basket bars, the single-sleeve bars they do not replace, and |ρ| ≤ 0.30 with the ten. The pooled null uses the same clock, a random evening and the same pair.

risks: Cost dependence: the cost filter means the trades taken follow Dukascopy's own night spreads, and FP's spreads on these crosses are unverified. The ReleveFP check and the reported break-even cost are mandatory before any real use.

The design leaves out the vendors' core hour (17:00-18:00 New York). A fail does not refute rollover-hour scalping, and a pass validates no vendor. Only neighbour 2 touches that hour, priced with unverifiable spreads.

The basket principle may be contested. Leaving out the AUD/NZD crosses drops vendor favourites such as EURAUD, where an edge might live. Adding the four dollar pairs widens 'crosses' to all pairs of Europe and North America.
The 25 % concentration bar stays hard even with ten pairs: a real, even effect at t = 2.5 passes it only about 31 % of the time (synthetic). A modest true effect could fail on concentration alone.

For the first 100 minutes, the band includes quotes from the rollover hour (16:20-18:00), and 18:00 is the CME reopen, whose first moves may be news rather than noise. The 19:00 neighbour reports this but cannot rescue the main.
The strict every-signal bar (all qualifying signals, overlaps allowed) can fail even when the one-trade-per-night rule works. This strictness is intended and declared.

Correlated exposure: ten pairs built from five currencies. At 7 % risk per trade, one bad night could cost a large part of the 1,000 EUR account. The rule only reports this; sizing is decided after a pass.
The lab's merge drops 'flat' minutes (unchanged bid), which at night can hide ask-only moves. A short's stop on the ask could be missed in rare cases; coverage is reported.
Tail evenings stay in the test: the GBP flash crash (2016-10-06, about 19:07 New York) falls inside the window and hits four GBP pairs.
The commission conversion for the crosses is fixed (EUR 1.05, GBP 1.20, CAD 0.70 USD) and only approximate. FP's commission for a EUR account must be read in MT5.
Multiple testing: seven configurations, after several earlier FX ideas. A pass is weaker evidence than it reads.
Regime change after 2021: vendors report bad years in 2022-2023. Only the single declared look can show it.
Implementation risk: new frames for six crosses, a custom pooled null and two stress readings. This is mitigated by the synthetic, truncation and hand checks and by the independent attack.
The live records that motivated the idea (683917 and others) lie mostly in 2022-2026. They set no number here, but a reviewer may still see indirect leakage.
The research notes cited in the addendum are in the session scratch folder, which can be cleared. A copy should be kept in the repository if the citation must stay valid.
